text: I think part of it is also just saying, "We don't have to be hesitant to jump into these problems.
speaker: Zoelle Egner
context: Lenny asks Zoelle what she learned from building VaccinateCA, a volunteer organization that helped people find COVID vaccine locations during the pandemic. VaccinateCA was created when vaccine availability was extremely chaotic, with different eligibility rules at every location. Zoelle explains that they built a simple system using phones, Discord, and Airtable to help hundreds of volunteers call vaccine locations and create a comprehensive database. She's sharing lessons about how tech can solve important problems without being overly complex.
text_ko: 제 생각에는 그 일부분은 "이런 문제들에 주저하지 말고 바로 뛰어들어도 된다"고 말하는 것 같아요.
text_zh: 我觉得有一部分就是要说，我们不必犹豫，直接去解决这些问题。
text_es: Creo que parte de esto también es decir: "No tenemos por qué dudar en entrar de lleno en estos problemas."
key_sentence: We don't have to be hesitant to jump into these problems.
original_text: I think part of it is also just saying, "We don't have to be hesitant to jump into these problems. It's important to engage with experts in the field, is not to say that tech solutionism is always the answer." And again, this is not super sophisticated technology, but because we were able to go in and talk to the people who are actually affected, get into the system that already existed, and make something really simple, really fast, it actually did have a huge difference and that's really exciting.

vocabulary.definition: Uncertain or reluctant to act or decide; showing indecision.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being hesitant can hinder decision-making processes, particularly in fast-paced environments where timely actions are crucial for success.
vocabulary.nuance: While hesitation can indicate caution and thoroughness, it may also suggest a lack of confidence or fear of making mistakes.

vocabulary.definition: To engage in an activity or situation suddenly and without hesitation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups, 'jumping into' challenges can reflect a proactive approach to problem-solving, encouraging teams to tackle issues head-on rather than delaying action.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase often carries a connotation of enthusiasm and readiness, but it can also imply a lack of preparation or forethought if used indiscriminately.

vocabulary.definition: Difficulties or challenges that require resolution or management.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, identifying and addressing problems is essential for maintaining operational efficiency and achieving strategic goals.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'problems' can sometimes carry a negative connotation, but in a business environment, it can also be viewed as opportunities for improvement and innovation.

text: I think if you have an authentic mission and people aren't just like, "Oh, sure, okay. You're connecting the world." But really it's some telephony startup. Like, "Okay." If people feel like it's genuinely authentic to what you're building, it can be incredibly meaningful.
speaker: Zoelle Egner
context: Lenny and Zoelle are discussing how having a compelling mission makes it much easier for startups to hire talent. Zoelle had just explained how VaccinateCA attracted hundreds of volunteers because the mission was so clear and meaningful. They're talking about the difference between companies with genuine, impactful missions versus those with generic or manufactured mission statements that don't truly reflect what the company does.
text_ko: 제 생각엔 미션이 진짜라면 사람들이 '아, 그래. 세상을 연결한다는 거구나' 하고 겉으로만 수긍하는 수준이 아니어야 해요. 반대로 실은 텔레포니 스타트업(telephony startup) 같은 거라면 사람들도 '음, 알겠어' 하고 그냥 넘어가죠. 사람들이 그 미션이 당신이 실제로 만들고 있는 것과 진심으로 맞닿아 있다고 느끼면, 그건 엄청 의미가 있어요.
text_zh: 我觉得如果你有一个真正的使命感，而不是让人觉得"哦好吧，你们说是要连接世界"，但实际上就是个电话技术的创业公司，这样的话人们会想"得了吧"。如果大家觉得你做的事情确实跟你在构建的东西是一致的、是发自内心的，那这个意义就太大了。
text_es: Creo que si tienes una misión auténtica y la gente no dice simplemente "Ah, sí, claro. Estás conectando el mundo" cuando en realidad es solo una startup de telefonía. Como que "Bueno, está bien." Si la gente siente que realmente es genuino lo que estás construyendo, puede ser increíblemente significativo.
key_sentence: Authentic missions can be incredibly meaningful, beyond just connecting the world.

vocabulary.definition: Genuine and true to its origins; not false or copied.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, an authentic mission resonates with stakeholders and customers, fostering trust and loyalty towards the brand or organization.
vocabulary.nuance: While often used positively to describe brands or missions, overuse can lead to skepticism if authenticity is perceived as marketing jargon.

vocabulary.definition: Having significance or purpose; conveying a sense of importance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups, creating meaningful products or services can lead to deeper connections with customers and a stronger market position.
vocabulary.nuance: The term is often used to highlight the emotional or social impact of a business initiative, distinguishing it from purely transactional interactions.

vocabulary.definition: A newly established business, typically in the early stages of development and often focused on innovative products or services.
vocabulary.businessContext: Startups are often characterized by their pursuit of rapid growth and scalability, frequently seeking venture capital to fund their operations.
vocabulary.nuance: While the term generally refers to new businesses, it can also imply a culture of innovation and risk-taking, which may not apply to all new ventures.

text: I think I repeated the same three talking points about why what we were doing mattered 5,000 times. Cannot overemphasize how many times I said the same stuff, and so did every other member of the board.
speaker: Zoelle Egner
context: Lenny asks Zoelle about the second lesson she learned from running VaccinateCA. Zoelle is explaining the critical importance of constantly repeating key messages when managing a large, diverse group of volunteers. VaccinateCA had hundreds of volunteers from different backgrounds joining and leaving at different times, making clear communication essential. She's emphasizing how leaders must be willing to repeat the same core messages thousands of times to keep everyone aligned.
text_ko: 우리가 하는 일이 왜 중요한지에 대한 같은 세 가지 요점을 5,000번은 반복한 것 같아요. 제가 같은 얘기를 몇 번이나 했는지를 아무리 강조해도 지나치지 않아요. 다른 이사회 구성원들도 모두 마찬가지였어요.
text_zh: 我把说明为什么我们做这事重要的那三条谈话要点(talking points) 说了不下五千遍。怎么强调都不为过——我反复讲同样的话，董事会(board)上的其他成员也是一样。
text_es: Creo que repetí las mismas tres ideas sobre por qué lo que hacíamos importaba unas 5.000 veces. No exagero: lo dije una y otra vez, y el resto del consejo hizo lo mismo.
key_sentence: Cannot overemphasize how many times I said the same stuff, and so did every other member of the board.
original_text: I think I repeated the same three talking points about why what we were doing mattered 5,000 times. Cannot overemphasize how many times I said the same stuff, and so did every other member of the board. It really is important and people will fill in the blanks with totally wild things if you don't continuously have that discipline of repeating yourself.

vocabulary.definition: To give excessive importance or attention to something, often to the point of distortion.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, overemphasizing certain aspects can lead to miscommunication or skewed perceptions of a project's significance.
vocabulary.nuance: While it can be useful to highlight key points, overemphasizing may detract from other important elements and can be perceived as insincere.

vocabulary.definition: Key messages or arguments that are prepared in advance to guide discussions or presentations.
vocabulary.businessContext: Talking points are often used in meetings, presentations, or public speaking to ensure that essential information is communicated clearly and effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: While talking points can help maintain focus, relying too heavily on them may lead to a lack of spontaneity and engagement in conversations.

text: So if you can be like, "Here are three templates that a person you might be excited about." That can be really helpful.
speaker: Zoelle Egner
context: Lenny asks Zoelle about her thoughts on the power and importance of templates for software companies, noting that many companies now create templates because they see how successful they were for Airtable and Notion. Zoelle is explaining that templates can be valuable for helping horizontal products (those that can be used for many different purposes) narrow down the use cases for users, but many companies misunderstand their primary purpose and expect them to drive new customer acquisition.
text_ko: 그래서 "여기 누군가가 관심을 가질 만한 템플릿(templates) 세 가지 있어요"라고 말해주면 정말 도움이 돼요.
text_zh: 如果你能这么说：“给你三套你可能会感兴趣的模板(templates)”，那真的很有帮助。
text_es: Así que, si puedes decir algo como: «Aquí tienes tres plantillas que podrían entusiasmar a esa persona», eso puede ser de gran ayuda.
key_sentence: Here are three templates that a person you might be excited about.
original_text: So if you can be like, "Here are three templates that a person you might be excited about." That can be really helpful. Where people sometimes get confused about templates, or have the wrong expectations about templates, is when they think that templates are going to be an acquisition mechanism, and they don't build in the foundation that is necessary for that to be true.

vocabulary.definition: Templates are pre-designed formats or structures that serve as a starting point for creating documents, presentations, or other materials.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, templates streamline processes by providing standardized formats that enhance efficiency and consistency in communication and documentation.
vocabulary.nuance: While templates imply a degree of uniformity, they can also be customized, allowing for creativity within a structured framework.

text: What it is good for is credibility. And that's where, if you have really clear goals, and you know how you are ready to leverage the asset of a piece of PR coverage, then it can be helpful to you.
speaker: Zoelle Egner
context: Lenny asks Zoelle about her potentially "spicy" take on launches and PR for early-stage startups. Zoelle has just explained that PR is generally not effective for getting leads or users directly, since most people won't click through from articles or remember to search for the company later. She's now explaining what PR is actually useful for and providing specific, measurable ways startups can leverage PR coverage effectively.
text_ko: 그게 좋은 건 신뢰도(credibility)를 쌓는 데요. 목표가 정말 분명하고, 한 건의 PR 보도(PR coverage)를 자산으로 어떻게 활용할지 준비가 되어 있다면 도움이 될 수 있어요.
text_zh: 它能带来的就是可信度。关键是，如果你目标很清楚，并且知道怎么把一则公关报道(PR coverage)利用好，那它就能帮到你。
text_es: Sirve para dar credibilidad. Y ahí es donde, si tienes objetivos muy claros y sabes cómo sacar partido al activo que supone una cobertura mediática (PR coverage), puede resultarte útil.
key_sentence: Leverage the asset of PR coverage to improve response rates for cold outbound.
original_text: What it is good for is credibility. And that's where, if you have really clear goals, and you know how you are ready to leverage the asset of a piece of PR coverage, then it can be helpful to you. So the two goals I always recommend to founders when thinking about using PR, are either hiring or maybe improving the response rate for your cold outbound.

vocabulary.definition: The quality of being trusted and believed in; the reliability of a source or information.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, credibility is essential for building trust with clients, investors, and stakeholders, often influencing decision-making and brand reputation.
vocabulary.nuance: Credibility often implies a long-term perception based on consistent performance and integrity, making it crucial in high-stakes environments.

vocabulary.definition: The strategic use of resources or advantages to maximize outcomes or influence.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, leveraging can refer to utilizing assets, relationships, or market positions to enhance profitability or competitive advantage.
vocabulary.nuance: Leverage often carries a connotation of strategic manipulation or optimization, and should be used carefully to avoid implications of exploitation.

vocabulary.definition: Any resource owned by an individual or entity that is expected to provide future economic benefits.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, assets can include tangible items like property and equipment, as well as intangible items like intellectual property and brand reputation.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'asset' often implies value and potential for generating income, and is commonly used in financial statements and investment discussions.

vocabulary.definition: Specific, measurable objectives that individuals or organizations aim to achieve within a defined timeframe.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, clear goals are crucial for guiding strategy, measuring performance, and aligning team efforts towards common outcomes.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'goals' can refer to both short-term and long-term objectives, they should be specific and actionable to be effective in a professional context.

text: Minimally. I'll say, if you care about this, send me a message. I will give you some advice. All of our industry will be better if there are more people working on customer success. So I will help you. Send me a note.
speaker: Zoelle Egner
context: Lenny asks Zoelle for resources that founders can use to learn how to invest in customer success early, since she had just recommended that B2B companies hire customer success before sales (which Airtable did). Zoelle explains that while there are many resources for customer success professionals, there aren't enough resources specifically aimed at helping founders understand how to set up and utilize customer success teams effectively.
text_ko: 간단히 말하면요. 이 주제에 관심 있으시면 저에게 메시지 보내세요. 몇 가지 조언을 드릴게요. 고객 성공(customer success) 분야에서 일하는 분들이 더 많아지면 우리 업계 전체가 좋아질 거예요. 그래서 제가 도와드릴게요. 편하게 연락 주세요.
text_zh: 简单说：如果你关心这事，给我发消息，我可以给你一些建议。要是行业里有更多人做客户成功（customer success），我们整个行业都会更好。所以我愿意帮你，给我发条消息吧。
text_es: En pocas palabras: si esto te interesa, escríbeme y te daré algunos consejos. Nuestro sector saldrá ganando si más personas trabajan en éxito del cliente (customer success), así que cuentas con mi ayuda.
key_sentence: If you care about this, send me a message; there's not a ton available.
original_text: Minimally. I'll say, if you care about this, send me a message. I will give you some advice. All of our industry will be better if there are more people working on customer success. So I will help you. Send me a note. Otherwise, I'll try and dig out some other things and maybe you can share them, but there's not a ton.

vocabulary.definition: Customer success refers to the proactive approach of ensuring that customers achieve their desired outcomes while using a product or service.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, customer success teams focus on building relationships with clients to enhance satisfaction, retention, and overall value derived from the product.
vocabulary.nuance: This term emphasizes a partnership with customers rather than a transactional relationship, making it particularly relevant in subscription-based or service-oriented industries.

vocabulary.definition: An industry is a distinct group of businesses or organizations that produce similar goods or services within an economy.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding the industry is crucial for businesses to identify market trends, competition, and opportunities for innovation and growth.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a broader economic sector or a more specific niche, so context is important when discussing industry dynamics.
